# Streaming and event ordering

What each pipeline operation may do to a stream, and what a consumer may conclude from the order it observed events in. The classes are v0.4.1 Appendix E; the ordering contract is v0.4.1 §27. Both are rendered from `docs/spec/hardening/streaming_classification.yaml`, which is also what `explain` reads and what the gate compares the command contracts against.

## Classes

| Class | Appendix E | Requires finite input | May materialize |
|---|---|---|---|
| `item_transform` | Item transform | no | no |
| `predicate` | Predicate | no | no |
| `prefix` | Prefix | no | no |
| `incremental_aggregate` | Incremental aggregate | no | no |
| `global_reorder` | Global reorder | yes | yes |
| `global_grouping` | Global grouping | yes | yes |
| `explicit_collect` | Explicit collect | yes | yes |
| `live_view` | Live view | no | no |

**`item_transform`** — One value in, zero or more values out, with no state that grows. `each` and projection. §25.2 forbids it capturing its complete input, which is what makes it this class rather than a collector wearing its name.

**`predicate`** — A test applied to each value in turn. `where`.

**`prefix`** — Answers from a bounded prefix of its input and then stops reading, which is what lets `source | take 1` complete while the source is still waiting (§60.1).

**`incremental_aggregate`** — Folds its input into state of a fixed or explicitly bounded size — a counter, an accumulator, a ring buffer of a declared length. Appendix E permits "constant/bounded state only", so a stage that grows its state per value is not this class however it is named.

**`global_reorder`** — Emits the same values in an order it can only know once it has them all. `sort`.

**`global_grouping`** — Emits one value per group, which it can only close once the input has ended. `group`.

**`explicit_collect`** — Holds a collection because its answer is defined over the whole of it: an explicit list, an exact percentile, the side of a relational operation that is not streamed past.

**`live_view`** — Maintains a bounded model of current state and repaints it. Never accumulates history: a live view that kept every frame would be §65.7's background collection with a picture on it.

|---|---|
| `ono.data.each` | `item_transform` |
| `ono.data.select` | `item_transform` |
| `ono.data.where` | `predicate` |
| `ono.data.take` | `prefix` |
| `ono.data.skip` | `prefix` |
| `ono.data.count` | `incremental_aggregate` |
| `ono.data.reduce` | `incremental_aggregate` |
| `ono.data.tail` | `incremental_aggregate` |
| `ono.data.sort` | `global_reorder` |
| `ono.data.group` | `global_grouping` |
| `ono.data.measure` | `explicit_collect` |
| `ono.data.join` | `explicit_collect` |

| `ono.place.map` | `live_view` |

## Event ordering

**Within one channel.** Total. Every event of one channel is delivered in the order it was produced, and no stage reorders its own channel: values keep value-channel order and partial failures keep error-channel order, however many stages they pass through (§27.1).

**Between the two kinds.** None. `StreamEvent` does not promise a total temporal ordering between independently produced value and partial-error channels unless a producer explicitly serializes them through one event source (§27.2).

**Causality.** Consumers MUST NOT infer causality from the relative observation order of a value and an asynchronously reported partial error. That a failure was observed after a value does not mean it happened after it, and a consumer that acts on the difference is reading the scheduler rather than the pipeline (§27.2).

**When a total order is part of the answer.** A provider or operation whose semantic contract must express "the error occurred between value A and value B" emits an ordered event stream through one sequence-bearing path — one sink, one send at a time, on one channel — rather than relying on scheduling between two channels (§27.3). `StreamSink::send_in_sequence` is that path: it places every event on the value channel, carrying a failure as the error value it is, so the order the producer chose is the order the consumer observes.

| Channel | Carries | Ordered within itself |
|---|---|---|
| `value` | The values a stage produced. | yes |
| `partial_failure` | Failures that concern one item rather than the pipeline, which spec §16.5 forbids collapsing into the result. | yes |

**`value`** — The stream's answer. A stage forwards these in the order it received them unless its own contract reorders — `sort` does, and says so in its classification above.

**`partial_failure`** — Reported beside the values rather than instead of them, and asynchronously: the stage that raised one keeps running, so the failure reaches the consumer when the error channel has room rather than at the position in the value sequence where it arose.
